UPSTREAM: soc/intel/skylake: Remove incorrect ME PG-status print As per discussion with CSME team, ME is NOT using PCI Config Space register HFSTS2 Bit 10 to update ME power-gated status. ME goes to CM0-PG state after ME device becomes idle after Bit 2 of MMIO register offset 0x800 (D0i3 Control - HECI1_D0I3C) is being set. And to retrieve the PG status of ME, one should read from the PWRMBASE+offset 0x590 (which should give the value 0xF9) and PWRMBASE+offset 0x594 (which should give the value 0xFF). But, also it needs some time for the ME FW to go to idle state and reflect these values in PWRMBASE registers after D0i3 bit is being set. This does not happen instantly. So, in coreboot, if we read the ME PG state in finalize.c, which happens just after FSP Notify phase, where actually ME D0i3 bit is set, we do not read the correct PG state values (i.e, 0xF9 and 0xFF). But, once it boots to Kernel, if we read those same registers through iotool mmio_read32 command, we get correct values. So, removing the ME PG state prints from coreboot, since it is actually showing wrong information, although ME Power Gating is successful. BUG=none BRANCH=none TEST=none Change-Id: I9d87531344a1935a70f66d66affd2893113dd1fc Signed-off-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@google.com> Original-Commit-Id: a1af090002193ef5f202b605397af067ce15caa2 Original-Change-Id: Idd31a9803b4c9db7d4bb8bbec5374583a8df0c41 Original-Signed-off-by: Barnali Sarkar <barnali.sarkar@intel.com> Original-Reviewed-on: https://review.coreboot.org/20172 Original-Tested-by: build bot (Jenkins) <no-reply@coreboot.org> Original-Reviewed-by: Aaron Durbin <adurbin@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/593547 Commit-Ready: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Tested-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org>

factory: add FlattenGroup Sometimes we want to define a group of tests but don't want to put them in an additional layer. For example, in Components test group, we put a small stress test + countdown test. Without FlatttenGroup, the test list structure will be: Components |-- Wifi |-- Probing |-- Bluetooth `-- StressGroup |-- Countdown `-- StressAppTest This prevents the Components group running in parallel. With FlattenGroup, you can do the following: "StressGroup": { "inherit": "FlattenGroup", "subtests": [ "Countdown", "StressAppTest" ] } And the Components group will be resolved to: Components |-- Wifi |-- Probing |-- Bluetooth |-- Countdown `-- StressAppTest Also, allowing a FlattenGroup can reduce the number of layers shown on UI, makes the UI more clean. BUG=b:31678190 TEST=make test, manual Change-Id: I1292f0655cdcfbdd5fdc16961fa8331e710bcfd8 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/593487 Commit-Ready: Wei-Han Chen <stimim@chromium.org> Tested-by: Wei-Han Chen <stimim@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Pi-Hsun Shih <pihsun@chromium.org>
